'''Karl Gustav Jöreskog''' (born 25 April 1935) is a [[Sweden|Swedish]] [[statistician]]. Jöreskog is a professor emeritus at [[Uppsala University]], and a co-author (with Dag Sörbom) of the [[LISREL]] statistical program. He is also a member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]]. Jöreskog received his bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees at [[Uppsala University]]. He is also a former student of [[Herman Wold]]. He was a statistician at [[Educational Testing Service|Educational Testing Service (ETS)]] and a visiting professor at [[Princeton University]].

==Research==
Jöreskog proposed a reliable numerical method for computing [[maximum-likelihood]] estimates in [[factor analysis]]; similarly reliable methods were also proposed by Gerhard Derflinger, Robert Jennrich, and Stephen M. Robinson at roughly the same time. Jöreskog's [[Fortran]] codes helped to popularize factor analysis around the world. While working at the [[Educational Testing Service]] and giving lectures at Princeton University, Jöreskog proposed a linear model for the analysis of covariance structures, a fundamental contribution to [[Structural equation modeling|structural equation modeling (SEM)]].

His other research interests include [[multivariate analysis]], [[item response theory]],  [[computational statistics|statistical computing]], and factor-analysis in [[geology]].

==Awards==
*In 1974 he was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].<ref>[http://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm View/Search Fellows of the ASA] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616161612/https://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm |date=2016-06-16 }}, accessed 2016-08-20.</ref>
*In 2007 Jöreskog received the Award for distinguished scientific applications of psychology<ref>Karl G. Jöreskog: Award for Distinguished Scientific Applications of Psychology. ''American Psychologist, 62,'' 768-769.</ref> from the [[American Psychological Association]] (APA).
*In 2004 he was awarded [[The Rudbeck Medal]]<ref>[http://www.uu.se/en/about-uu/traditions/prizes/rudbeck-medal/ The Rudbeck Medal]</ref> by Uppsala University.
